observation: Legacy v0.6 inclusion verification did not bind the declared leaf index to proof orientation; valid proofs could be relabeled to any in-range index.
prior_belief: v0.6 inclusion was a useful baseline but its proof geometry was less strict than v0.7 consistency semantics.
intervention: Added RFC 9162 index/size-derived proof orientation and exact geometry verification as an isolated v0.8 layer.
measured_outcome: 8,256 valid inclusion proofs passed; 3,500 property attacks and 1,500 hostile attacks rejected; 42/42 legacy false-index relabels rejected by v0.8.
evidence_quality: Strong local/RFC-aligned, synthetic; external sibling transfer absent.
confidence_delta: Increased confidence in inclusion index/geometry binding only; no change to external trust or semantic truth confidence.
failure_or_surprise: v0.6 accepted every false in-range index relabel in the seven-leaf probe.
reusable_lesson: A verifier must derive path orientation from authenticated structural coordinates; range-checking an index is not the same as binding the proof to that index.
invalidated_assumption: A valid root reconstruction plus an in-range declared index is sufficient proof of position.
retry_condition: Re-run if hash algorithm, proof schema, tree shape, or adapter backend changes.
expiration_or_revalidation_condition: Real signed sibling evidence or RFC/implementation discrepancy appears.
next_experiment: Version-pinned adapter upgrade or real-manifest end-to-end transfer, whichever becomes available first.
